title: graph
instructions: This server stores entities as bundles of components. Use graph_schema to see the available components and their properties; use graph_query or graph_show to read them, and graph_apply to write changes.

graph_apply.title: Apply atomic changes
graph_apply.description: Create, edit, link or trash entities atomically via edits/links, q, bundles, or id/text (path defaults to doc.body). Ids accept eids, human ids and names; $name creates an entity reusable within this call. Omitted fields stay; null clears properties/components. Text edits replace literal find (one match unless all), then prepend/append; reads are guarded automatically, with optional was tokens. links add relations the store declares; drop removes them. q patches one entity: T-12 .doc.title="New title" !blocked; $new .task creates one. The array argument is bundles (not entities): [{entity:{eid},component:{fields}}], $was guards and $delete moves an entity and its deletion cascade to recoverable trash. graph_trash reads saved deletions; graph_restore restores them. Returns applied bundles with resolved ids, $alias and stamps. check previews then rolls back; reuse $names, since preview ids are temporary. Name only components and properties graph_schema lists; a guessed name is refused. https://yaks.app/docs/store

q.description: One entity patch; quote spaced values: T-12 .doc.title="two words". Values follow schema types; null clears (even quoted), !component removes. $name or fresh UUID creates.

bundles.description: Atomic array of entity bundles (argument name bundles, not entities): [{"entity":{"eid":"$new"},"doc":{"title":"…"}}]. eid accepts existing id/name or new $name; edges derive theirs from ends.

set.description: Dotted fields or whole components, e.g. {"doc.title":"New","blocked":null}.

path.description: Text property, e.g. doc.body or content.body.

was.description: Read tokens keyed by dotted field path.

edits.description: Changes to any entities, applied together.

id.description: Entity to replace text on; $name creates.

path.description: Text property for id/text; default doc.body.

branch.description: Write on this branch (branch_list) rather than main; main never sees it.

graph_query.title: Query entities
graph_query.description: Query .component.property=value with & (and), | (or), bare search words, presence .component/!component (a kind's name reads as the components the kind is), or ?component to include without filtering. A name alone is a component, so always qualify a property with its component: .app.version, never .version. q is the whole query, with no .where or .query around it, e.g. .doc.title~=recipe&.created.at>2026-11-01 .order=-created.at .limit=5. Each store has its own components: call graph_schema first and name only what it lists. It reads live entities only: a deleted one has no component to query, and there is no .tombstone. Every row is an entity, so .entity alone names nothing: a query names the components its rows carry. Filter by id with .entity.eid=T-12, .entity.eid=#3b5bc70420, or .eid=T-12. Supply an id after =. graph_show reads entities by id. Operators: != ~= < >, lists a,b, ranges 1..9. To match part of a value, ~= (.web.url~=cloudflare); there is no bare ~. To find text by its words, use bare search words; by meaning, .near=T-12. Use .order=doc.title to sort by a property. Use .fields=doc.title to return one property or .fields=doc to return the whole component. Other directives include .limit=20 and .refs=T-12. filters narrow all of q. Returns named components; * or no named component returns whole entities. Bare search defaults to 20 compact hits. doc.body includes $was. graph_show reads whole entities. A guessed name is refused with the declared names nearest it. A query has no .timing: timing: true answers with where the call's time went, the Server-Timing line yak --timing prints. https://yaks.app/docs/querying

q.description: Query, e.g. .task.status=open&.doc.title~=recipe; ~= matches part of a value, and there is no bare ~.

fields.description: What each row carries, as .fields= takes it: doc.title,created.at or a whole component.

branch.description: Read on this branch (branch_list) rather than main.

timing.description: Answer with where the call's time went, as Server-Timing entries (the line yak --timing prints), beside the rows.

graph_show.title: Show entities
graph_show.description: Read whole entities by eid, human id (T-12), a short handle (#3b5bc70420 or unambiguous bare hex 3b5bc70420), or name, once each: id for one, ids for several. $was.doc.body holds its SHA-256 for guarded writes. Missing ids are reported; all missing refuses. Backlinks: graph_query .refs=<id>; text search: search.

branch.description: Read on this branch (branch_list) rather than main.

graph_trash.title: Read graph trash
graph_trash.description: Read recoverable graph deletions, grouped by deletion id and time, with their saved bundles. Omit ids to list the trash; ids selects groups containing those entity eids. id reads one group; after continues after the last group id returned. Returned bundles are saved snapshots, not live entities. graph_restore restores a deletion. Permanent purging requires the person's confirmation page.

ids.description: Deleted entity eids; omit to list the trash.

id.description: One saved deletion group id; ignores paging.

after.description: Continue after this saved deletion group id.

graph_schema.title: Read the schema

app.doing: Checking what the data looks like…
app.done: Checked what the data looks like

graph_schema.description: Read vocabulary JSON Schema. No arguments returns a component/property index; component returns full declarations, types, refs and write examples. When a name is absent, the tool looks for those words in the vocabulary's names and descriptions. kind returns its definition and associated components, taking precedence over component; a kind's name sent as component is that kind. https://yaks.app/docs/components

search.title: Search text
search.description: Search indexed words and, with vectors, meaning. Ranked compact bundles contain entity.eid and hit:{id,title,kind,excerpt,source}; source is text, meaning or both. In excerpts, \u0001/\u0002 delimit matches. graph_show reads whole entities. https://yaks.app/docs/querying

graph_restore.title: Restore graph trash
graph_restore.description: Restore one saved deletion by id, or the newest deletions containing ids (entity eids), including their deletion cascades. Supply id or ids. Restore missing entities, components and properties while preserving later live values. Returns applied bundles. Read graph_trash first to choose the deletion. Permanent purging requires the person's confirmation page.

id.description: One saved deletion group id from graph_trash, including an older group.
